question: When white light is passed through a prism it undergoes dispersion. The angle of deviation is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**inversely proportional to the wavelength**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When white light passes through a prism, it splits into its constituent colors due to dispersion.
 
• The angle of deviation for each color depends on its wavelength.
 
• The angle of deviation is inversely proportional to the wavelength of the light.
 
• This means that light with a shorter wavelength (e.g., violet) deviates more than light with a longer wavelength (e.g., red).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dispersion of Light**

 
 
• Dispersion occurs when light separates into its component colors due to different degrees of refraction for different wavelengths.
 
• The refractive index of the material of the prism varies with wavelength, causing different colors to bend by different amounts.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength and Frequency**
 
 
• Wavelength is the distance between successive crests of a wave, typically measured in meters.
 
• Frequency is the number of waves that pass a point in one second, measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
• The speed of light (c) is the product of its wavelength (λ) and frequency (f): c = λf.
 
 
 
• **Prism**
 
 
• A prism is a transparent optical element with flat, polished surfaces that refract light.
 
• The most common type of prism is a triangular prism, used to disperse light into a spectrum of colors.
